A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same self-certainty and Borda-voting work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical reasoning, code reasoning, and code generation experiments, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds reward-model comparisons, voting analyses, and measurements relating self-certainty to question difficulty.

M1.justification: Uniform-to-model KL averaging and Borda weights remain. However, v2's distributional equations replace conditioning on y<i with y≤i, while retaining the preceding-token sequence definition. The PDFs do not resolve whether this changes the scored token positions or introduces an indexing inconsistency.

E1.justification: Both versions use LiveBench-Math, GSM8K, MATH, CRUXEval-O, and LiveCodeBench, including MATH difficulty subsets and training-derived token frequencies. The added analyses remain within these datasets and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds GRM-Llama3.2-3B-RewardModel-FT and Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B comparisons on GSM8K and CRUXEval-O in Table 1. It expands perplexity comparisons beyond LiveBench-Math, compares confidence metrics within Borda voting in Table 5, and adds normalized weighted-sum self-consistency in Appendix B.6. This substantially broadens the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: Retained experiments keep the stated sampling settings, candidate counts, answer masking, and dataset splits. New appendix protocols measure mean confidence by difficulty and correctness using 64 responses per question and compare voting variants on MATH-Level5, with N=64 specified for Table 6. These are additional evaluation designs, not established reruns of earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2 newly examines confidence versus question difficulty; B.5 tests confidence-metric choice within Borda voting; B.6 compares probability and self-certainty scoring with their voting variants. These substantially extend analysis of the metric and aggregation contributions. Earlier length, oracle, difficulty-stratified accuracy, empirical-distribution, and case-study analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repetitions for the main confidence-measure experiment and single trials for the reasoning-model and empirical-distribution experiments. New appendix analyses also use single-trial reporting. No new seed-reporting or uncertainty-estimation practice is introduced.

E6.justification: Existing table entries and matched figure values are retained, but substantial results are added. Table 1 reports GSM8K N=64 accuracy of 95.15% for PRM versus 91.07% for the best Borda setting. Table 6 reports MATH-Level5 N=64 accuracy of 38.75% for normalized weighted-sum selection versus 39.43% for self-certainty with Borda. Table 5 adds metric-specific voting scores, and Figure 10 adds difficulty-confidence trends. v1's below-2% Level1 no-answer statistic is omitted.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 derives the self-certainty gradient and its directional change under target-token log-likelihood ascent. It adds Theorem A.1's condition p_target > sum(p_k^2), a proof, an argmax corollary, and qualifications about initial decreases. v1 contains metric definitions but no corresponding theorem or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: efficient reward-free self-certainty, scalable Best-of-N selection, complementary Borda voting, and applicability to open-ended generation. Rewording and additional support do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds a conditional training-based rationale in Section 3.4 and proposes self-certainty as a difficulty estimator in Appendix B.2. Section 7 reframes underperformance against self-consistency as complementarity and adds soft self-consistency and reward-shaping applications. v1's explanation linking no-answer frequency to model capacity is removed.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses NVIDIA A100 hardware, identifies the evaluated reward-model checkpoints and access references, and recommends tuning the Borda exponent on a small task-specific validation set. These additions improve documentation without establishing changes to earlier experimental settings. The project code link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Geng et al.'s confidence-estimation survey, GRM and Qwen PRM references, and Wang et al.'s soft self-consistency work, while removing Liang et al.'s internal-consistency survey. Discussion of normalized weighted-sum self-consistency and potential soft self-consistency applications extends positioning without changing the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, model background, results discussion, and future-work sections are extensively condensed and rewritten. Appendices are reorganized around a new theoretical section, and the acknowledgment is removed. This constitutes substantial language and narrative revision even though the abstract and conclusion largely persist.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a two-column layout to a single-column NeurIPS format, with widespread resizing and relocation of displays and reflowing of examples. Original Tables 1 and 2 exchange numbering and placement. v2 expands the benchmark table, adds Figure 10 and Tables 5–6, and relabels Figure 8's DC entries as SCe without changing their values.

improvement.justification: Direct reward-model and normalized weighted-sum comparisons fill gaps in v1's empirical support, while targeted voting analyses clarify the contributions of scoring and aggregation. These provide a limited net gain. The benefit is constrained by Table 1's Borda-best caption contradicting its PRM results, unexplained conditioning-index changes, and the new Corollary A.2's false strict-inequality claim for uniform distributions.
